sanskrit: mātā jānāti yad gotraṃ mātā jānāti yasya saḥ mātur bharaṇamātreṇa prītiḥ snehaḥ pituḥ prajāḥ
english: The mother knows the lineage; the mother knows whose son he is. For her mere act of bearing him there is love, while the father's affection toward his offspring rests on trust alone.

sanskrit: pāṇibandhaṃ svayaṃ kṛtvā sahadharmam upetya ca yadi yāpyanti puruṣāḥ striyo nārhanti yāpyatām
english: Having of their own will taken her hand in marriage and entered upon a shared duty with her, if men then drive their women away, those women do not deserve to be cast off.

sanskrit: bharaṇād dhi striyo bhartā pātyāc caiva striyāḥ patiḥ guṇasyāsya nivṛttau tu na bhartā na patiḥ patiḥ
english: For a man is a woman's bhartṛ because he supports her, and her pati because he protects her; but when these virtues fail in him, he is neither her supporter nor her protector nor her lord.

sanskrit: evaṃ strī nāparādhnoti nara evāparādhyati vyuccaraṃś ca mahādoṣaṃ nara evāparādhyati
english: Thus the woman commits no offense; it is the man alone who offends; and in committing a grave transgression, it is the man alone who is at fault.

sanskrit: striyā hi paramo bhartā daivataṃ paramaṃ smṛtam tasyātmanā tu sadṛśam ātmānaṃ paramaṃ dadau sarvakāryāparādhyatvān nāparādhyanti cāṅganāḥ
english: For a woman's husband is her highest lord, declared to be her supreme deity; and she has given her very self, a self equal to his own, as the highest gift. Since in all matters the fault falls upon the man, women themselves commit no offense.

sanskrit: yaś canokto hi nirdeśaḥ striyā maithunatṛptaye tasya smārayato vyaktam adharmo nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: And as for any command not spoken yet pressed upon a woman for the sating of lust, in him who would so remind her there is plainly unrighteousness; of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: yāvan nārīṃ mātaraṃ ca gaurave cādhike sthitām avadhyāṃ tu vijānīyuḥ paśavo 'py avicakṣaṇāḥ
english: That a woman, and above all a mother set in the highest reverence, is not to be slain—this even brute beasts, lacking all discernment, understand.

sanskrit: devatānāṃ samāvāyam ekasthaṃ pitaraṃ viduḥ martyānāṃ devatānāṃ ca snehād abhyeti mātaram
english: They know the father to be the gathering of all the gods made one; yet out of the affection that belongs to mortals and to gods alike, one turns toward the mother.

sanskrit: evaṃ vimṛśatas tasya cirakāritayā bahu dīrghaḥ kālo vyatikrāntas tatas tasyāgamat pitā
english: As Cirakārin pondered thus at length, in keeping with his slow-acting nature, a long stretch of time passed by; and then his father came to him.

sanskrit: medhātithir mahāprājño gautamas tapasi sthitaḥ vimṛśya tena kālena patnyāḥ saṃsthāvyatikramam
english: Medhātithi, the deeply wise Gautama, steadfast in austerity, had in that interval reflected upon the breach of his wife's conduct.

sanskrit: so 'bravīd duḥkhasaṃtapto bhṛśam aśrūṇi vartayan śrutadhairyaprasādena paścāttāpam upāgataḥ
english: Scorched by grief, shedding tears in plenty, and brought through the calm grace of learning and fortitude to remorse, he spoke.

sanskrit: āśramaṃ mama saṃprāptas trilokeśaḥ puraṃdaraḥ atithivratam āsthāya brāhmaṇaṃ rūpam āsthitaḥ
english: "Purandara, lord of the three worlds, came to my hermitage; taking up the guise of a guest, he assumed the form of a brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: samayā sāntvito vāgbhiḥ svāgatenābhipūjitaḥ arghyaṃ pādyaṃ ca nyāyena tayābhipratipāditaḥ
english: He was soothed with fitting and gracious words, honored with a welcome, and by her, in due form, was offered the guest-water and the water for his feet.

sanskrit: paravaty asmi cāpy uktaḥ praṇayiṣye nayena ca atra cākuśale jāte striyo nāsti vyatikramaḥ
english: Told, 'I am subject to another,' yet he said, 'I shall press my suit by craft.' In the misfortune that arose from this, the woman bears no transgression.

sanskrit: evaṃ na strī na caivāhaṃ nādhvagas tridaśeśvaraḥ aparādhyati dharmasya pramādas tv aparādhyati
english: Thus neither the woman, nor I, nor that wandering lord of the gods has sinned against dharma; it is heedlessness alone that has done the wrong.

sanskrit: īrṣyājaṃ vyasanaṃ prāhus tena caivordhvaretasaḥ īrṣyayā tv aham ākṣipto magno duṣkṛtasāgare
english: The seers who have raised their seed on high call jealousy a born vice; and I, hurled down by jealousy, am sunk in the ocean of evil deeds.

sanskrit: hatvā sādhvīṃ ca nārīṃ ca vyasanitvāc ca śāsitām bhartavyatvena bhāryāṃ ca ko nu māṃ tārayiṣyati
english: Should I slay a virtuous woman, and a wife condemned only out of my own vice, a wife who is mine to cherish and sustain—who then will carry me across?"

sanskrit: antareṇa mayājñaptaś cirakārī hy udāradhīḥ yady adya cirakārī syāt sa māṃ trāyeta pātakāt
english: "Cirakārin, whom I commanded in a moment's haste, is noble of mind; if today he be true to his slow-acting way, he will save me from this sin.

sanskrit: cirakārika bhadraṃ te bhadraṃ te cirakārika yady adya cirakārī tvaṃ tato 'si cirakārikaḥ
english: O Cirakārika, blessings on you—blessings on you, O Cirakārika! If today you are still slow to act, then you are truly Cirakārika.

sanskrit: trāhi māṃ mātaraṃ caiva tapo yac cārjitaṃ mayā ātmānaṃ pātakebhyaś ca bhavādya cirakārikaḥ
english: Save me, and your mother too, and the austerity I have amassed, and your own self from sins—be this day Cirakārika!

sanskrit: sahajaṃ cirakāritvaṃ ciraprājñatayā tava saphalaṃ tat tavādyāstu bhavādya cirakārikaḥ
english: Slow-acting is your inborn way, joined to a wisdom that takes its time; let it bear fruit for you today—be this day Cirakārika!

sanskrit: ciram āśaṃsito mātrā ciraṃ garbheṇa dhāritaḥ saphalaṃ cirakāritvaṃ kuru tvaṃ cirakārika
english: Long were you longed for by your mother, long carried in her womb; make your slow-acting nature bear fruit, O Cirakārika!

sanskrit: cirāyate ca saṃtāpāc ciraṃ svapiti vāritaḥ āvayoś cirasaṃtāpād avekṣya cirakārika
english: Out of anguish he lingers long; restrained, he sleeps long—consider the long anguish of us both, O Cirakārika!"

sanskrit: evaṃ sa duḥkhito rājan maharṣir gautamas tadā cirakāriṃ dadarśātha putraṃ sthitam athāntike
english: Thus grieving, O king, the great seer Gautama then beheld his son Cirakārin standing close at hand.

sanskrit: cirakārī tu pitaraṃ dṛṣṭvā paramaduḥkhitaḥ śastraṃ tyaktvā tato mūrdhnā prasādāyopacakrame
english: And Cirakārin, seeing his father in deepest grief, cast aside his weapon and, bowing his head, set about winning his father's favor.

sanskrit: gautamas tu sutaṃ dṛṣṭvā śirasā patitaṃ bhuvi patnīṃ caiva nirākārāṃ parām abhyagaman mudam
english: And Gautama, seeing his son fallen with his head upon the ground, and his wife unharmed, came to the highest joy.

sanskrit: na hi sā tena saṃbhedaṃ patnī nītā mahātmanā vijane cāśramasthena putraś cāpi samāhitaḥ
english: For that great-souled one had not driven his wife to ruin, dwelling as he did in the solitude of the hermitage; and his son too had been composed.

sanskrit: hanyāt tv anapavādena śastrapāṇau sute sthite vinītaṃ praśnayitvā ca vyavasyed ātmakarmasu
english: He might have slain her without reproach, with his son standing weapon in hand; yet, the boy having humbly asked his counsel, he could now resolve upon his own course of action.

sanskrit: buddhiś cāsīt sutaṃ dṛṣṭvā pituś caraṇayor natam śastragrahaṇacāpalyaṃ saṃvṛṇoti bhayād iti
english: And seeing his son bowed at his feet, the thought came to him: 'Out of fear he is concealing the rashness of having taken up the weapon.'

sanskrit: tataḥ pitrā ciraṃ stutvā ciraṃ cāghrāya mūrdhani ciraṃ dorbhyāṃ pariṣvajya ciraṃ jīvety udāhṛtaḥ
english: Then the father praised him long, long kissed him upon the head, long held him in both arms, and uttered, 'Live long!'

sanskrit: evaṃ sa gautamaḥ putraṃ prītiharṣasamanvitaḥ abhinandya mahāprājña idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Thus that deeply wise Gautama, filled with love and gladness, embraced his son and spoke these words.

sanskrit: cirakārika bhadraṃ te cirakārī ciraṃ bhava cirāyamāṇe tvayi ca ciram asmi suduḥkhitaḥ
english: "O Cirakārika, blessings on you—be ever slow to act, and live long! Yet while you tarried, I was long and grievously stricken with sorrow."

sanskrit: gāthāś cāpy abravīd vidvān gautamo munisattamaḥ cirakāriṣu dhīreṣu guṇoddeśasamāśrayāt
english: And the learned Gautama, best of sages, also spoke these verses, founded on the recital of the virtues of the steadfast slow-acting ones.

sanskrit: cireṇa mitraṃ badhnīyāc cireṇa ca kṛtaṃ tyajet cireṇa hi kṛtaṃ mitraṃ ciraṃ dhāraṇam arhati
english: "Slowly should one bind a friend, and slowly cast off a friendship once made; for a friend made slowly deserves to be kept long.

sanskrit: rāge darpe ca māne ca drohe pāpe ca karmaṇi apriye caiva kartavye cirakārī praśasyate
english: In passion, in arrogance, in pride, in enmity, in sinful deeds, and in any unkind act that must be done, the slow-acting man is praised.

sanskrit: bandhūnāṃ suhṛdāṃ caiva bhṛtyānāṃ strījanasya ca avyakteṣv aparādheṣu cirakārī praśasyate
english: In the unproven offenses of kinsmen, of friends, of servants, and of womenfolk, the slow-acting man is praised."

sanskrit: evaṃ sa gautamas tasya prītaḥ putrasya bhārata karmaṇā tena kauravya cirakāritayā tayā
english: Thus, O Bhārata, that Gautama was pleased with his son for that deed, O Kaurava—pleased by that very slowness to act.

sanskrit: evaṃ sarveṣu kāryeṣu vimṛśya puruṣas tataḥ cireṇa niścayaṃ kṛtvā ciraṃ na paritapyate
english: So a man who reflects in all his undertakings, and after long deliberation comes to a decision, does not grieve for long thereafter.

sanskrit: ciraṃ dhārayate roṣaṃ ciraṃ karma niyacchati paścāttāpakaraṃ karma na kiṃ cid upapadyate
english: He holds his anger long in check, long restrains his action, and no deed that breeds remorse befalls him.

sanskrit: ciraṃ vṛddhān upāsīta ciram anvāsya pūjayet ciraṃ dharmān niṣeveta kuryāc cānveṣaṇaṃ ciram
english: Long let him wait upon his elders, long attend and honor them; long let him practice the duties of dharma, and long pursue his inquiry.

sanskrit: ciram anvāsya viduṣaś ciraṃ śiṣṭān niṣevya ca ciraṃ vinīya cātmānaṃ ciraṃ yāty anavajñatām
english: Long attending upon the wise, long serving the cultured, and long disciplining himself, a man comes in time to a state beyond contempt.

sanskrit: bruvataś ca parasyāpi vākyaṃ dharmopasaṃhitam ciraṃ pṛcchec ciraṃ brūyāc ciraṃ na paribhūyate
english: Even when another utters words bound up with dharma, let him question long and answer long; thus he is never long despised.

sanskrit: upāsya bahulās tasminn āśrame sumahātapāḥ samāḥ svargaṃ gato vipraḥ putreṇa sahitas tadā
english: Having dwelt for many years in that hermitage, the brāhmaṇa of mighty austerities then went to heaven, together with his son.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kathaṃ rājā prajā rakṣen na ca kiṃ cit pratāpayet pṛcchāmi tvāṃ satāṃ śreṣṭha tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: How should a king protect his subjects and yet cause no one distress? I ask you, best of the good; tell me that, grandfather.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam dyumatsenasya saṃvādaṃ rājñā satyavatā saha
english: Bhīṣma said: On this too they recite an ancient tale—the dialogue of Dyumatsena with King Satyavat.

sanskrit: avyāhṛtaṃ vyājahāra satyavān iti naḥ śrutam vadhāya nīyamāneṣu pitur evānuśāsanāt
english: Satyavat spoke what had not been spoken before—so we have heard—when, by his own father's order, certain men were being led away to execution.

sanskrit: adharmatāṃ yāti dharmo yāty adharmaś ca dharmatām vadho nāma bhaved dharmo naitad bhavitum arhati
english: "Righteousness passes into unrighteousness, and unrighteousness into righteousness, if killing were to be called a duty—this ought not to be."

sanskrit: dyumatsena uvāca atha ced avadho dharmo dharmaḥ ko jātu cid bhavet dasyavaś cen na hanyeran satyavan saṃkaro bhavet
english: Dyumatsena said: If non-killing were the law, then what could ever count as duty at all? If robbers were never slain, O Satyavat, a ruinous confusion would arise.

sanskrit: mamedam iti nāsyaitat pravarteta kalau yuge lokayātrā na caiva syād atha ced vettha śaṃsa naḥ
english: 'This is mine'—such a claim would have no force in the age of Kali, and the very course of worldly life could not go on. If you know otherwise, declare it to us.

sanskrit: satyavān uvāca sarva eva trayo varṇāḥ kāryā brāhmaṇabandhanāḥ dharmapāśanibaddhānām alpo vyapacariṣyati
english: Satyavat said: All three of the lower orders should be made to hold fast to the brāhmaṇas; and of those bound by the cords of dharma, only a few will go astray.

sanskrit: yo yas teṣām apacaret tam ācakṣīta vai dvijaḥ ayaṃ me na śṛṇotīti tasmin rājā pradhārayet
english: Whichever of them should transgress, let the twice-born point him out, saying, 'This man will not heed me'; upon such a one let the king sit in judgment.

sanskrit: tattvābhedena yac chāstraṃ tat kāryaṃ nānyathā vadhaḥ asamīkṣyaiva karmāṇi nītiśāstraṃ yathāvidhi
english: What the scripture lays down in accord with the truth of each case—that must be carried out; killing is not to be ordered otherwise, nor deeds done without examining them by the science of statecraft as ordained.

sanskrit: dasyūn hinasti vai rājā bhūyaso vāpy anāgasaḥ bhāryā mātā pitā putro hanyate puruṣe hate pareṇāpakṛte rājā tasmāt samyak pradhārayet
english: When a king slays robbers, more often than not he destroys the guiltless along with them; for when a man is killed, his wife, mother, father, and son are killed in him. Therefore, where one man has wronged another, let the king judge with care.

sanskrit: asādhuś caiva puruṣo labhate śīlam ekadā sādhoś cāpi hy asādhubhyo jāyate 'śobhanā prajā
english: An evil man may one day come to good character; and even from the good, born of those who are evil, there may spring an unworthy offspring.

sanskrit: na mūlaghātaḥ kartavyo naiṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ api khalv avadhenaiva prāyaścittaṃ vidhīyate
english: No root-and-branch slaughter should be carried out; that is not the eternal law. Indeed, even without killing, expiation may be prescribed.

sanskrit: udvejanena bandhena virūpakaraṇena ca vadhadaṇḍena te kleśyā na puro 'hitasaṃpadā
english: By rebuke, by imprisonment, by disfigurement, and by the punishment of death are such men to be afflicted, but not at once with the full measure of harm.

sanskrit: yadā purohitaṃ vā te paryeyuḥ śaraṇaiṣiṇaḥ kariṣyāmaḥ punar brahman na pāpam iti vādinaḥ
english: When, seeking refuge, they come round to the royal chaplain, saying, 'Brāhmaṇa, we shall do no sin again,'

sanskrit: tadā visargam arhāḥ syur itīdaṃ nṛpaśāsanam bibhrad daṇḍājinaṃ muṇḍo brāhmaṇo 'rhati vāsasam
english: then they deserve to be released—such is the king's ordinance. A brāhmaṇa, shaven and bearing the staff and deerskin, is worthy to receive a fresh garment of pardon.

sanskrit: garīyāṃso garīyāṃsam aparādhe punaḥ punaḥ tathā visargam arhanti na yathā prathame tathā
english: For graver and graver offenses, repeated again and again, men deserve release—but not in the same measure as at the first.

sanskrit: dyumatsena uvāca yatra yatraiva śakyeran saṃyantuṃ samaye prajāḥ sa tāvat procyate dharmo yāvan na pratilaṅghyate
english: Dyumatsena said: Wherever the people can be held within their bounds by a compact, that is called dharma—but only so long as it is not overstepped.

sanskrit: ahanyamāneṣu punaḥ sarvam eva parābhavet pūrve pūrvatare caiva suśāsyā abhavañ janāḥ
english: But if no one were ever put to death, everything would fall into ruin. In the earlier ages, and in those still earlier, the people were easy to govern.

sanskrit: mṛdavaḥ satyabhūyiṣṭhā alpadrohālpamanyavaḥ purā dhigdaṇḍa evāsīd vāgdaṇḍas tadanantaram
english: Gentle they were, abounding in truth, with little malice and little wrath. Of old the only chastisement was a word of reproach; next came rebuke by speech.

sanskrit: āsīd ādānadaṇḍo 'pi vadhadaṇḍo 'dya vartate vadhenāpi na śakyante niyantum apare janāḥ
english: Then there came also the penalty of confiscation; and today the penalty of death prevails. Yet there are some men who cannot be restrained even by death.

sanskrit: naiva dasyur manuṣyāṇāṃ na devānām iti śrutiḥ na gandharvapitṝṇāṃ ca kaḥ kasyeha na kaś cana
english: There is no robber of men alone, says the sacred lore, nor of the gods alone, nor of the gandharvas and the ancestors alone; for here in the world, who is anything to anyone, and who is no one at all?

sanskrit: padmaṃ śmaśānād ādatte piśācāc cāpi daivatam teṣu yaḥ samayaṃ kuryād ajñeṣu hatabuddhiṣu
english: One takes a lotus even from a cremation ground, and a deity's emblem even from a demon. As for those who are ignorant and bereft of sense—who could make a binding compact with such men?

sanskrit: satyavān uvāca tān na śaknoṣi cet sādhūn paritrātum ahiṃsayā kasya cid bhūtabhavyasya lābhenāntaṃ tathā kuru
english: Satyavat said: If you cannot bring such men to goodness without violence, then make an end of them—but in such a way that there is some gain for someone, present or yet to come.

sanskrit: dyumatsena uvāca rājāno lokayātrārthaṃ tapyante paramaṃ tapaḥ apatrapanti tādṛgbhyas tathāvṛttā bhavanti ca
english: Dyumatsena said: For the sake of the world's order kings undergo the highest austerity; they feel shame before such righteous men and so come to act righteously themselves.

sanskrit: vitrāsyamānāḥ sukṛto na kāmād ghnanti duṣkṛtīn sukṛtenaiva rājāno bhūyiṣṭhaṃ śāsate prajāḥ
english: Holding evildoers in dread, the well-doers do not slay them from mere desire; for the most part kings govern their subjects by virtue alone.

sanskrit: śreyasaḥ śreyasīm evaṃ vṛttiṃ loko 'nuvartate sadaiva hi guror vṛttam anuvartanti mānavāḥ
english: Thus the world follows the better conduct of the better man; for men ever follow the conduct of their superior.

sanskrit: ātmānam asamādhāya samādhitsati yaḥ parān viṣayeṣv indriyavaśaṃ mānavāḥ prahasanti tam
english: Him who, without composing himself, would set others in order, while he is yet a slave to his senses amid objects of desire—at such a man men laugh.

sanskrit: yo rājño dambhamohena kiṃ cit kuryād asāṃpratam sarvopāyair niyamyaḥ sa tathā pāpān nivartate
english: Whoever, out of pride and delusion, does anything unfitting toward the king, is to be restrained by every means; thus does he turn back from sin.

sanskrit: ātmaivādau niyantavyo duṣkṛtaṃ saṃniyacchatā daṇḍayec ca mahādaṇḍair api bandhūn anantarān
english: He who would curb wrongdoing must first curb his own self; and he should chastise with heavy punishments even his nearest kinsmen.

sanskrit: yatra vai pāpakṛt kleśyo na mahad duḥkham archati vardhante tatra pāpāni dharmo hrasati ca dhruvam iti kāruṇyaśīlas tu vidvān vai brāhmaṇo 'nvaśāt
english: Where the doer of evil who deserves affliction meets no great suffering, there sins multiply and dharma surely dwindles—so the learned brāhmaṇa, of compassionate nature, gave his instruction.

sanskrit: iti caivānuśiṣṭo 'smi pūrvais tāta pitāmahaiḥ āśvāsayadbhiḥ subhṛśam anukrośāt tathaiva ca
english: In just this way, my son, I have been instructed by my forefathers and grandsires, who out of tenderness reassured me again and again.

sanskrit: etat prathamakalpena rājā kṛtayuge 'bhajat pādonenāpi dharmeṇa gacchet tretāyuge tathā dvāpare tu dvipādena pādena tv apare yuge
english: This rule the king observed in its full first form in the Kṛta age; with dharma diminished by a quarter he proceeded so in the Tretā age, with dharma upon two feet in the Dvāpara, and upon a single foot in the latter age.

sanskrit: tathā kaliyuge prāpte rājñāṃ duścaritena ha bhavet kālaviśeṣeṇa kalā dharmasya ṣoḍaśī
english: And so, when the Kali age has come, through the misconduct of kings and by the peculiar working of time, only a sixteenth part of dharma may remain.

sanskrit: atha prathamakalpena satyavan saṃkaro bhavet āyuḥ śaktiṃ ca kālaṃ ca nirdiśya tapa ādiśet
english: Now if one were to follow the first rule in full, O Satyavat, confusion would arise; therefore, marking out a man's span of life, his strength, and the times, the king should prescribe his penance.

sanskrit: satyāya hi yathā neha jahyād dharmaphalaṃ mahat bhūtānām anukampārthaṃ manuḥ svāyaṃbhuvo 'bravīt
english: For the sake of truth, that one might not here forsake the great fruit of dharma, and out of compassion for living beings, Manu, son of the Self-Existent, declared this.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca avirodhena bhūtānāṃ tyāgaḥ ṣāḍguṇyakārakaḥ yaḥ syād ubhayabhāg dharmas tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: That renunciation which, without doing harm to living beings, fosters the sixfold policy—the dharma that partakes of both worldly life and renunciation—tell me of that, grandfather.

sanskrit: gārhasthyasya ca dharmasya tyāgadharmasya cobhayoḥ adūrasaṃprasthitayoḥ kiṃ svic chreyaḥ pitāmaha
english: Of the duty of the householder and the duty of renunciation, both of which set out toward a goal not far apart—which, grandfather, is the more excellent?
